goal: Close canonical-backlog churn by making refresh and reconciliation paths semantically and byte-idempotent while excluding transient operational projections from canonical task state.
scope: control-plane backlog persistence and refresh/reconciliation mutation paths
transient readiness, batch, and attempt projection boundaries
out_of_scope: changing task dependency, admission, authority, or verification policy
removing canonical workflow status or evidence state
architecture_constraints: canonical backlog owns durable task intent and workflow/evidence state
readiness reasons, batch IDs, and last-attempt IDs are operational projections and must not persist in canonical task records
operational state remains caller-supplied and separate from canonical backlog truth
semantic writes remain atomic and secret-safe
repeated refresh and reconciliation after convergence must preserve bytes and revision
acceptance_criteria: all mutating refresh/reconciliation paths are audited for transient task projections
canonical persistence strips stale readiness_reasons, batch_id, and last_attempt_id projections
refresh_readiness returns readiness projections without persisting them
batch and attempt lifecycle state remains in operational state while canonical status/evidence state remains durable
the exact AC-DEV-019 run pattern has regression coverage for transient-field absence and repeated byte identity
canonical backlog semantics and unrelated task bytes are preserved within the accepted persistence contract
validation: focused persistence and control-plane regression tests
full Python test suite and documentation validation
backlog/passport JSON validation and git diff --check
